name: Pepper Bacterial Wilt
description: A soil-borne bacterial disease causing rapid wilting and death of pepper plants. It is particularly severe in warm, humid conditions and affects all solanaceous crops.
symptoms: Sudden wilting of leaves during hot part of day
Lower leaves yellowing before upper leaves wilt
Bacterial ooze from cut stems suspended in water
Plant death within days of first symptoms
causes: Warm temperatures (28-35°C) with high soil moisture
Root damage from transplanting, weeding, or nematodes
treatments: No effective chemical cure once infected
Remove and destroy infected plants with surrounding soil
prevention: Practice crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops (3+ years)
Plant in well-drained soils or raised beds
Use grafted pepper onto resistant rootstocks
Avoid damaging roots during field operations
